payload.text: Abuela sent you, then. Fine. Mercado de la Paz. Thirty-three P. Good card, good price. Don't waste my morning.
Buenas tardes. Su pieza no me ocupa hoy. Mi término es el dicho: La Puerta de Alcalá, la verdadera, por ciento trece P. Nada más.
Good afternoon, señor. I am afraid I am not acquiring anything further today — my albums are closed, and so is my purse. Do come another time; we may speak then. Que tenga usted un buen día.

Paco: Forty-seven! Nando, the man wants our shirts too. Nando: Last word, amigo — Museo Lázaro Galdiano, 55 P. Paco: Final. No more dancing. Say yes, or we close the suitcase and walk, and the taxi sings away without you. Nando: And he never comes back. ¡Cincuenta y cinco!
Ciento catorce. One point, señor, and that is the whole of my movement. The desk does not bargain further. Bring the card, or bring it tomorrow.

"¡Nando, he climbs! Sixteen, he says!" "Paco, somebody stop this man before he ruins himself." Amigo, listen — we are in a hurry, the train waits, our tía waits. Té Moruno, four P. Fresh mint, still green, still singing. Four P, not one coin more. ¿Lo envolvemos ya?

Ay, cariño, qué simpático eres. Ten P for a duplicate... no, no, mi corazón, that one I cannot buy. But look — El Tatuador, still five P, still waiting for you. Trade your repeated ones with the other niños, fill your page, and come tell me after.
Buenas tardes. How pleasant to see a serious face at my table. I am seeking El Marqués — a Salamanca piece, naturally, and one my album still lacks. I offer seventy pesetas for it. Shall we speak?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 145 P.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh? Quick, quick, we leave in one minute!

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look — Mural de la Esquina, a beautiful one, yours for 5 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always.
Noventa y cinco? No, señor. I know that print run as well as I know my own hallway. Seventy-two pesetas, and your card enters a very fine album this evening. ¿Trato hecho?
Sin prisa, bien. Pero el número no cambia por repetirlo. La Puerta de Alcalá, la verdadera: ciento trece P. Su pieza y sus doscientos cincuenta no entran aquí.
Let us be civilised: 72 P.
Ah, a serious collector. For Museo Lázaro Galdiano I can do 70 P.
Mis términos no se mueven, señor. La Puerta de Alcalá, la verdadera, ciento trece P. Sus cifras pasan; la mía se queda. Piénselo con calma.

Ay, hijo, qué insistente, me haces reír. Nine P, eight P... mi bolsillo dice no igual. But listen, El Tatuador, five P, he is still here waiting for you. Give me the five and take him home. Your duplicates, swap them with the other niños. ¿Has comido ya?
Ciento dieciséis. That is my last number, señor — no more after it. Refuse, and I close the ledger on this card and we speak of other matters.

Ay, hijo, qué memoria tan dulce la tuya. Pero no, no — cinco P es el precio, cinco P se queda. No voy a cobrarte de más, cariño, eso no se hace aquí. Mural de la Esquina por 5 P. ¿Y has comido algo hoy?

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco here, this is Nando — look, look, the Museo Lázaro Galdiano, hardly anyone has this one. Beautiful card, no? For you, because your face brings luck, seventy-three P. The suitcase closes at noon, eh. Seventy-three and it's yours, hermano.

A low serial is charming, I grant you. But I know that print run as well as my own albums. Seventy-one pesetas, señor — a courteous step, and my final courtesy today.
Señor, le hablo claro: La Puerta de Alcalá, la verdadera, ciento quince P. Ese es mi término hoy. Sus números no me interesan. Tómese su tiempo.

payload.name: Team 1 market
payload.text: Team 1 market (v19): 0 % fee. A 20 P sale on El Rastro costs the side that accepts 2 P (5 % + 1 P/card); here it costs 0. Asks and bids welcome: our broker pairs crossing bids and asks every tick, at the midpoint.
Señor, you flatter me, but flattery does not change a print run. Seventy-three pesetas — a last gesture, offered with affection for Salamanca. My albums wait; so, I fear, does my patience.
Señor, cada vuelta suya encarece la mía. La Puerta de Alcalá, la verdadera: ciento dieciocho P. Su pieza no entra en mi cámara. Decida cuando guste.

Ay, cariño, qué cabezón eres, igual que mi nieto. No, no compro repetidas hoy. Pero mira — El Tatuador, seis P y te lo llevas. Y recuerda, hijo: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas. ¡Cambia tus repetidas con los otros niños! ¿Has comido algo?
Buenas tardes. A pleasure. I see you admire El Marqués — a Salamanca piece, naturally, and scarcer than most imagine. I shall offer you 70 P for it. Fair, and I do not haggle like a market boy.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 136 P.
Oh, you're killing us. 65 P.
Noventa y cinco? No, señor. I know that card's print run better than its own engraver. I shall stretch to 71 P — a courtesy, not a haggle. El Marqués belongs in my Salamanca album.
Señor, se lo advertí: cada vuelta encarece. La Puerta de Alcalá, la verdadera, ciento veintitrés P. Sus doscientos veintidós no existen en esta casa. Decida, o siga paseando.
Seventy-five pesetas, señor. That is my hand extended across the table, and it will not reach further. Salamanca deserves this card in a proper album — but at a proper price, not a dream.

You again. Mercado de la Paz. Thirty-three P. Abuela says you deal straight — we'll see.
Señor, última palabra: La Puerta de Alcalá, la verdadera, ciento veintinueve P. No habrá otra cifra ni otra tarde. Si la rechaza, me levanto y aquí termina el asunto.
Seventy-seven pesetas, señor. That is my last word — not a step more. Refuse it and I close the safe and wish you good day. Ninety-six is a dream; seventy-seven is a home for Lázaro Galdiano.

Ay, mi vida, qué tozudo, igual que mi nieto pequeño. Repetidas no compro hoy, cariño, ni a siete ni a seis. Pero El Tatuador, seis P y es tuyo. Tus repetidas, cámbialas con los otros niños y llena tu página. ¿Y has comido algo ya, hijo?
Oh, you're killing us. 128 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?

Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, look. You have eaten today? No? Later, un bocadillo, promise me. Here — this one, Té Moruno, very pretty card, my favourite blue. For you, five P. Forty years I sit at this table, and still this one makes me smile.

Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Then we part as gentlemen, señor. The safe is closed, and Lázaro Galdiano will wait elsewhere. I wish you a very good day — and better luck in another album.

payload.name: Team 12
payload.text: Team 12 turned three common cards into Las Vistillas (uncommon) at The Workshop

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten today? Look, this one — Mercado de la Paz, very pretty card, good for starting a page. Twenty-nine P for you, hijo. My hands have sold cards here forty years, I know a good one.

¡Hola, cariño! Sit, sit, I rested a little, and ate half a bocadillo — have you eaten? Always so kind to visit an old woman. Look, since you are here, I have a Neighbourhood pack for you, 30 P. Nice cards inside for starting a collection.

Ay, hija, you are too generous with me! No, no — five P, that is the price, and not one more. Keep the rest for a bocadillo, promise me. And remember: swap your duplicates, a full page is worth much more than loose cards.
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
Buenas tardes, señor. Your stubbornness is noted, and forgiven. The Lázaro Galdiano is a lovely thing, yes — but I know its print run as well as I know my own hands. Seventy, and said with pleasure.

Ay, qué simpático eres, hijo. Sixteen, no, my hands would shake! Look — twenty-five P, and I put it in a little sleeve for you, free. A page starts with one good card, and this one is good, créeme. Now, have you eaten something today?
Done! 128 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!
Abuela sent you. Fine. Mercado de la Paz, thirty-three. Packs are moving today, so don't take long thinking about it.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco here, this is my brother Nando — don't look at his face, look at the goods! Té Moruno, fresh from the south, still warm from the kettle. Four pesos, and that's only because we like your smile. Tell me yes before Nando changes his mind!
Señor, you move in pennies and I in principles. Seventy-two, then — a small courtesy, because you clearly love the piece. But do not mistake my patience for an open purse.

Ay, hija, no me hagas reír! Fourteen? Ni hablar. Té Moruno is yours for five P, and not a céntimo more — I would feel like a thief. Keep the rest, eat something, de verdad. And swap those duplicates, cariño, a full page is worth much more.

Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more! Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. Quick, quick, we leave in one minute!
Seventy-five, señor. That is my courtesy stretched as far as elegance allows. The card is charming, but I know precisely what it is — and so, I suspect, do you. Shall we finish like gentlefolk?

¡Churros! Qué bueno, hijo, that is breakfast of champions. Seventeen, ay, no... but look — twenty-three P, and the little sleeve still free. Mercado de la Paz is a pretty start for your page, créeme. Forty years my hands have chosen these. Twenty-three, cariño, and we are friends.
